facts.name: Aethel
facts.desc: A blue-gray world ringed by the debris of three dead civilizations; its crust is laced with a luminous mineral the locals never named because naming it killed them.

facts.name: The Glass Sea
facts.desc: A continent-sized basin where an ocean was psychically boiled to vapor in a single afternoon; the seabed fused to black glass that still hums.

facts.name: The Sunken Choir Vault
facts.desc: A drowned cathedral-city beneath the Glass Sea, where the first miners stored what they pulled from the deep crust.

facts.name: The Hollow Spire
facts.desc: A kilometers-tall tower drilled down rather than up — a mineshaft turned monument, lined with the petrified bodies of those who refused to stop digging.

facts.name: Rookery of the Pale Wing
facts.desc: Cliffside roosts of a winged people who tried to flee the catastrophe by going up; their wings are fossilized mid-beat.

facts.name: The Quiet Orchard
facts.desc: A forest of crystalline trees grown from psychic coral; once a living archive, now silent except to those who can hear the dead.

facts.name: Bishop's Landing
facts.desc: The first human foothold on Aethel, built in the lee of the Hollow Spire by colonists who did not yet know what they were standing on.

facts.name: The Vael
facts.desc: A telepathic deep-ocean people who thought as one mind across the Glass Sea. They first found the singing mineral and learned it could amplify thought into force. They mined it to build a paradise of shared dreaming.

facts.name: The Delvers
facts.desc: A chitinous, sunless people who built downward. When the Vael's surface stocks ran low, the Delvers contracted to mine the deep seams — and bored straight into the thing the mineral was made from.

facts.name: The Pale Wing
facts.desc: A winged caste of oracles who read the future in the mineral's glow. They saw the catastrophe coming and sold prophecies of it instead of preventing it — until the day there was no future left to read.

facts.name: The Orchard Keepers
facts.desc: A slow, plant-mind species that recorded all history into living crystal trees. Neutral to the mining, they survived longest — long enough to encode the whole truth before the silence took them too.

facts.name: Aethel Survey Corps
facts.desc: The human expedition that arrived twelve thousand years after the fall, chasing the mineral as a power source — repeating the first mistake with better tools.

facts.name: Dr. Elara Myne
facts.desc: Lead of the Survey Corps; the first human to hear the mineral sing and not go mad. She suspects the artifacts are a warning, not a treasure.

facts.name: Commander Iben Tovar
facts.desc: Wants the mineral extracted on schedule. Believes the aliens died of weakness, not warning.

facts.name: Sefa
facts.desc: A colony-born child who dreams in Vael, decades before any human should be able to. The orchard answers her.

facts.name: Dreamtide
facts.desc: Vael shared-mind telepathy: many minds thinking as one wave. Amplified through the mineral, a wave could move matter.

facts.name: The Deep Sight
facts.desc: Pale Wing precognition — reading probable futures in the mineral's flicker. Reliable until the future itself collapsed.

facts.name: The Silence Touch
facts.desc: The catastrophe's signature: a psychic deadening that erases thought and memory from any mind near the wound in the crust.

facts.name: The Singing Is Alive
facts.desc: The Orchard Keepers' creed that the mineral was not ore but the dreaming body of a sleeping mind — and to mine it was to flay a god awake.

facts.name: The Unmaking Silence
facts.desc: The wound the mining opened never closed. It spreads slowly outward across the crust, eating thought, and the Survey Corps is digging toward its edge.

facts.name: The First Tuning Fork
facts.desc: The Vael's prototype amplifier — a fork of singing mineral that turned shared dreams into force. Found in the Sunken Choir Vault.

facts.name: Delver Core Sample
facts.desc: A sealed bore-core from the deepest shaft, still warm, with something curled at its heart that twitches when observed.

facts.name: The Last Prophecy Plate
facts.desc: A Pale Wing oracle-plate whose carved future trails off mid-glyph — the moment the Deep Sight saw nothing more.

facts.name: Orchard Memory Seed
facts.desc: A crystal seed from the Quiet Orchard holding the Keepers' final, complete account of the fall — playable only to a psychic ear.

facts.name: Vael Deathmask
facts.desc: A mineral mask worn by the last Vael speaker, fused to the face by the Silence Touch in the act of trying to warn the others.

facts.name: The Wingbone Key
facts.desc: A Pale Wing flight-bone carved into a key that opens the Hollow Spire's sealed bottom — the last thing the oracles tried to lock away.

facts.name: Sefa's River Stone
facts.desc: A polished shard the child Sefa carries; it grows warm near the buried wound and lets a human mind survive the Silence Touch, briefly.

facts.name: The Mineral Was A Mind
facts.desc: The singing mineral was the slow-dreaming body of a single planet-spanning consciousness sleeping in the crust. Every glowing seam was a nerve.

facts.name: The Vael Tapped Its Dreams
facts.desc: The Vael learned to draw force from the mineral by riding its dreams — harmless at first, like skimming a sleeper's warmth. They built a civilization on borrowed thought.

facts.name: The Delvers Cut To The Quick
facts.desc: When surface seams thinned, the Delvers bored into the deep cortex of the sleeping mind — and severed the nerves that kept it dreaming and not waking.

facts.name: The Mind Woke In Pain
facts.desc: The planet-mind woke mutilated, in agony, unable to understand the small thinking things crawling in its wounds. Its first reflex was to stop the pain — by stopping all thought near it.

facts.name: The Silence Spread Outward
facts.desc: The Silence Touch radiated from the wound, deadening every mind it reached. The Vael's shared dream went dark mid-thought; the Delvers froze in their tunnels; the Pale Wing's futures all ended at the same instant.

facts.name: The Keepers Recorded The End
facts.desc: Slow and rooted, the Orchard Keepers felt the Silence approach over years. They spent their last centuries encoding the whole chain into the crystal trees — a warning aimed at whoever came next. Then they, too, went quiet.

facts.name: The Dreaming Cities
facts.desc: Vael context lore: the cities of shared dream that the tuning fork made possible.

facts.name: The Speaker's Last Cry
facts.desc: Vael context lore: the final Vael speaker tried to broadcast a warning to the whole collective and was silenced mid-sentence.

facts.name: The Deep Contract
facts.desc: Delver context lore: the trade pact that sent the hive-engineers into the deep seams on the Vael's behalf.

facts.name: The Twitch In The Core
facts.desc: Delver context lore: the bore-core that still moves — a sliver of the mind's living tissue, never fully dead.

facts.name: The Oracles Who Sold The End
facts.desc: Pale Wing context lore: the seer-aristocracy monetized their visions of the coming silence rather than acting on them.

facts.name: The Sealing Of The Spire
facts.desc: Pale Wing context lore: with no future left to read, the oracles sealed the Hollow Spire to bury the deepest shaft.

facts.name: To Mine Is To Flay
facts.desc: Orchard context lore: the Keepers' belief that the mineral was a living mind, which the others dismissed as superstition.

facts.name: The Second Drilling
facts.desc: Human context lore: the Survey Corps's extraction plan unknowingly aims at the same nerve the Delvers severed.

facts.name: The Child Who Hears
facts.desc: Human context lore: Sefa dreams in Vael and the Orchard answers her, making her the only one who can read the Memory Seed.

facts.name: The First Tapping
facts.desc: The Vael draw force from the mineral for the first time and build the Dreaming Cities.

facts.name: The Deep Bore
facts.desc: The Delvers sever the deep nerves of the sleeping mind.

facts.name: The Waking
facts.desc: The planet-mind wakes in agony and looses the Silence Touch.

facts.name: The Great Silencing
facts.desc: The Silence spreads across the world, ending three civilizations within a generation.

facts.name: The Final Encoding
facts.desc: The Orchard Keepers commit the full history to the crystal trees and fall silent.

facts.name: The Human Arrival
facts.desc: The Survey Corps lands twelve thousand years later, chasing the same mineral.

facts.name: The Warning, Not The Treasure
facts.desc: The central arc: can the humans read the dead civilizations' warning before they re-open the wound?
